newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi denies Italy sought EMU slowdown with Spain.
newsitem.headline: Prodi denies Italy sought EMU slowdown with Spain.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi denied on Monday that he asked his Spanish counterpart Jose Maria Aznar for support to try to have the Maastricht criteria for entry into a single European currency softened.

A government statement said Prodi telephoned Aznar on Monday afternoon after the Financial Times quoted the Spanish leader as saying Italy wanted the two countries to "walk together holding hands towards Maastricht."

"(Prodi) reminded Aznar that, during the bilateral summit in Valencia, the porposals for collaboration between Italy and Spain referred to several sectors...and certainly not presumed joint actions to soften the Maastricht criteria," it said.

Prodi and Aznar met in Valencia earlier this month. The statement said Prodi used the meeting to underline Italy's determination to do everything to be in the first wave of countries launching the single currency in 1999.
Aznar told the Financial Times: "I am not interested in holding hands. I told him we'd be there right at the start."

Prodi's government unveiled a tougher-than-expected 1997 budget on Friday that aims to cut 62.5 trillion lire off next year's deficit and bring the debt-to-gross domestic product ration in line with the Maastricht targets.
Economic commentators said Prodi was forced to toughen up the package after Aznar refused to join Italy's tentative bid to persuade European partners to relax the stringent criteria.
